question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent line to the curve $f(x)=-7\operatorname{arccsc} x$ at $x=\sqrt{5}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arccsc} $ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccsc} x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-7\operatorname{arccsc} x) \\  & =-7\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\right) \\  & =\frac{7}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line to the curve $y=f(x)$ at $x=\sqrt{5}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\sqrt{5}) & =\frac{7}{|\sqrt{5}|\sqrt{{\sqrt{5}}^{2}-1}} \\  & =\frac{7}{\sqrt{5}\sqrt{5-1}} \\  & =\frac{7}{2\sqrt{5}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arccsc} $ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccsc} x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\sqrt{x}+5\operatorname{arccsc} x) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}+5\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccsc} x) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}+5\left(-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\right) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}-\frac{5}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arccot} $ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccot} x)=-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccot} x+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)) \\  & =-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}+\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+1} \\  & =\frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions

question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arccot} $ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccot} \,x)=-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x+\operatorname{arccot} x) \\  & =2+\left(-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\right) \\  & =2-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={y}^{′}(0) & =2-\frac{1}{1+{0}^{2}} \\  & =2-1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arccsc} $ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccsc} x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x}-2\operatorname{arccsc} x) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}-2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccsc} x) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}-2\left(-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\right) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}+\frac{2}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arccot} $ is

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}(\operatorname{arccot}  x) 	=  -\dfrac 1 {1+x^2}.
$$

Using the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\,\operatorname{arccot} x) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccot} x) \\  & =2\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\right) \\  & =-\frac{2}{1+{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Here, we let $u(x)=\operatorname{arccot} x$ and $v(x)={x}^{3},$ and apply the quotient rule.

We use the formulae

$$
{u}^{′}(x)=-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{and}\,{v}^{′}(x)=3{x}^{2}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\cdot {x}^{3}-\operatorname{arccot} x\cdot 3{x}^{2}}{({x}^{3})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{{x}^{3}}{1+{x}^{2}}-3{x}^{2}\operatorname{arccot} x}{{x}^{6}} \\  & =-\frac{\left(\frac{{x}^{3}+3(1+{x}^{2}){x}^{2}\operatorname{arccot} x}{1+{x}^{2}}\right)}{{x}^{6}} \\  & =-\frac{{x}^{3}+3(1+{x}^{2}){x}^{2}\operatorname{arccot} x}{{x}^{6}(1+{x}^{2})} \\  & =-\frac{x+3(1+{x}^{2})\operatorname{arccot} x}{{x}^{4}(1+{x}^{2})}.\end{aligned}
$$

{u}^{′}(x)=2x+4\,\text{and}\,{v}^{′}(x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(2x+4)\cdot \operatorname{arccsc} x-({x}^{2}+4x)\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\right)}{{\operatorname{arccsc} }^{2}x} \\  & =\frac{2x+4}{\operatorname{arccsc} x}+\frac{{x}^{2}+4x}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}\cdot {\operatorname{arccsc} }^{2}x}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Here, we let $u(x)={3}^{x}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{arccsc} \,x,$ and apply the quotient rule.

We use the formulae

$$
{u}^{′}(x)={3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{and}\,{v}^{′}(x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3)\cdot \operatorname{arccsc} \,x-{3}^{x}\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\right)}{{(\operatorname{arccsc} \,x)}^{2}}. \\  & ={3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot \frac{\operatorname{arccsc} \,x}{{(\operatorname{arccsc} \,x)}^{2}}+\frac{{3}^{x}}{{(\operatorname{arccsc} \,x)}^{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}} \\  & ={3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\frac{1}{\operatorname{arccsc} \,x}+\frac{{3}^{x}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\,\frac{1}{|x|{(\operatorname{arccsc} \,x)}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Here, we let $u(x)=\operatorname{arccot} x$ and $v(x)=x$, and apply the quotient rule.

We use the formulae

$$
{u}^{′}(x)=-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{and}\,{v}^{′}(x)=1.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\cdot x-\operatorname{arccot} x\cdot 1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{x}{1+{x}^{2}}-\operatorname{arccot} x}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{\left(\frac{x+(1+{x}^{2})\operatorname{arccot} x}{1+{x}^{2}}\right)}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{x+(1+{x}^{2})\operatorname{arccot} x}{{x}^{2}(1+{x}^{2})}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Here, we let $u(x) = \operatorname{arcsec}  x$ and $v(x) = \operatorname{arccsc}  x$, and apply the quotient rule.

We use the formulae

$$
u'(x) =  \dfrac 1 {|x| \sqrt {x^2 - 1}}	\quad \text{and} \quad	v'(x) = -\dfrac 1 {|x| \sqrt {x^2 - 1}}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\cdot \operatorname{arccsc} x-\operatorname{arcsec} x\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\right)}{{\operatorname{arccsc} }^{2}x} \\  & =\left(\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\right)\frac{\operatorname{arccsc} x+\operatorname{arcsec} x}{{\operatorname{arccsc} }^{2}x} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{arccsc} x+\operatorname{arcsec} x}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}{\operatorname{arccsc} }^{2}x}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arccsc} $ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccsc} {x}^{2}) & =-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the product rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccsc} {x}^{2})+\operatorname{arccsc} {x}^{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}\sqrt{{x}^{4}-1}}\right)+\operatorname{arccsc} {x}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =\operatorname{arccsc} {x}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x-\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x\sqrt{{x}^{4}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arccot} $ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccot} x)=-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the product rule, the formula above and the chain rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x\operatorname{arccot} {x}^{3}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccot} {x}^{3})+\operatorname{arccot} {x}^{3}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{3{x}^{2}}{1+{({x}^{3})}^{2}}\right)+\operatorname{arccot} {x}^{3}\cdot \left(\frac{1}{x}\right) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{arccot} {x}^{3}}{x}-\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{1+{x}^{6}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The formulae for the derivatives of $\operatorname{arccsc} $ and $\operatorname{arcsec} $ are

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccsc} x) & =-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsec} x) & =\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the product rule and the formulae above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\operatorname{arcsec} x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccsc} x)+\operatorname{arccsc} x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsec} x) \\  & =\operatorname{arcsec} x\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\right)+\operatorname{arccsc} x\cdot \left(\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\right) \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{arcsec} x}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}+\frac{\operatorname{arccsc} x}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{arccsc} x-\operatorname{arcsec} x}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arccot} $ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccot} \,x)=-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the product rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x}\cdot \operatorname{arccot} (\sqrt{x})) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x})\cdot \operatorname{arccot} (\sqrt{x})+\sqrt{x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccot} \,(\sqrt{x})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\cdot \operatorname{arccot} (\sqrt{x})+\sqrt{x}\cdot [-\frac{1}{1+{(\sqrt{x})}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x})] \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{arccot} (\sqrt{x})}{2\sqrt{x}}-\frac{\sqrt{x}}{1+x}\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{arccot} (\sqrt{x})}{2\sqrt{x}}-\frac{1}{2(1+x)}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The formulae for the derivatives of $arctan$ and $\operatorname{arcsec} $ are

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arctanx) & =\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsec} x) & =\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the chain rule and the formulae above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\operatorname{arcsec} ({x}^{2}))) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+(\operatorname{arcsec} ({x}^{2}))^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsec} ({x}^{2})) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+(\operatorname{arcsec} ({x}^{2}))^{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{|{x}^{2}|\sqrt{({x}^{2})^{2}-1}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+(\operatorname{arcsec} ({x}^{2}))^{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{|{x}^{2}|\sqrt{({x}^{2})^{2}-1}}\cdot 2x \\  & =\frac{2}{x\sqrt{{x}^{4}-1}(1+{\operatorname{arcsec} }^{2}({x}^{2}))}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arcsec} $ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsec} \,x)=\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5\operatorname{arcsec} ({x}^{2}+3)) \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{|{x}^{2}+3|\sqrt{({x}^{2}+3)^{2}-1}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+3) \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{|{x}^{2}+3|\sqrt{({x}^{2}+3)^{2}-1}}\cdot (2x) \\  & =\frac{10x}{|{x}^{2}+3|\sqrt{({x}^{2}+3)^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent line to the curve at $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(2) & =\frac{10(2)}{|{2}^{2}+3|\sqrt{({2}^{2}+3)^{2}-1}} \\  & =\frac{20}{|7|\sqrt{49-1}} \\  & =\frac{20}{7\sqrt{48}} \\  & =\frac{20}{7\cdot 4\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{5}{7\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{21}.\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent line to the function $y=\operatorname{arcsec} ({x}^{3}-6x)$ at $x=1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arcsec} $ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsec} x)=\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsec} ({x}^{3}-6x)) \\  & =\frac{1}{|{x}^{3}-6x|\sqrt{({x}^{3}-6x)^{2}-1}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}-6x) \\  & =\frac{1}{|{x}^{3}-6x|\sqrt{({x}^{3}-6x)^{2}-1}}\cdot (3{x}^{2}-6) \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}-6}{|{x}^{3}-6x|\sqrt{({x}^{3}-6x)^{2}-1}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line to the curve at $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(1)\text{ } & =\frac{3(1)^{2}-6}{|{1}^{3}-6(1)|\sqrt{({1}^{3}-6(1))^{2}-1}} \\  & =\frac{-3}{|-5|\sqrt{(1-6)^{2}-1}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{5\sqrt{24}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{5\sqrt{4\cdot 6}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{5\cdot \sqrt{4}\cdot \sqrt{6}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{5\cdot 2\cdot \sqrt{6}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{10\sqrt{6}} \\  & =-\frac{3\sqrt{6}}{10\sqrt{6}\cdot \sqrt{6}} \\  & =-\frac{3\sqrt{6}}{60} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{6}}{20}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arcsec} $ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsec} \,x)=\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\operatorname{arcsec} ({e}^{x})] \\  & =\frac{1}{|{e}^{x}|\sqrt{{({e}^{x})}^{2}-1}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x}) \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{x}\sqrt{{e}^{2x}-1}}\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2x}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent line to the curve at $x=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡10$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡10) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2(\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)/2)}-1}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡10}-1}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10-1}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions Using the Chain Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arccsc} $ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccsc} \,x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\operatorname{arccsc} (\sqrt{x})] \\  & =-\frac{1}{|\sqrt{x}|\sqrt{{(\sqrt{x})}^{2}-1}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}\sqrt{x-1}}\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2x\sqrt{x-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent line to the curve at $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(2) & =-\frac{1}{2\cdot 2\sqrt{2-1}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arccot} $ is

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}(\operatorname{arccot}  x) 	=  -\dfrac 1 {1+x^2}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\,\operatorname{arccot} ({x}^{2}+5)) \\  & =2\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{1+({x}^{2}+5)^{2}}\right)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+5) \\  & =-\frac{2}{1+({x}^{2}+5)^{2}}\cdot 2x \\  & =-\frac{4x}{1+({x}^{2}+5)^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{4x}{{x}^{4}+10{x}^{2}+26}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
